title: Conv2D and Max-Pooling from Scratch
summary: Implement the output-size formula, zero padding, a vectorized multi-channel conv2d with stride and padding, and max-pooling with its argmax-routing backward pass, checked against naive loop references.

ShapeMismatch.hint: Compute H_out and W_out with conv_output_size first, then make sure every reshape uses exactly N·H_out·W_out rows and C·KH·KW columns.

hints.test_output_size_formula: out = floor((in + 2·pad − kernel) / stride) + 1. Use integer division on the whole numerator, then add 1. If kernel > in + 2·pad there is no valid position. Raise ValueError.
hints.test_pad_input: np.pad(x, ((0, 0), (0, 0), (pad, pad), (pad, pad))). Batch and channel axes are never padded.
hints.test_conv_is_cross_correlation: Don't flip the kernel. out[i, j] = Σ x[i + u, j + v] · w[u, v], exactly like PyTorch's Conv2d.
hints.test_conv_matches_naive_reference: Each output sums over all input channels and the whole KH × KW window, then adds b[f].
hints.test_conv_stride_and_padding: Pad first. Output (i, j) reads the window starting at row i·stride, column j·stride of the padded input.
hints.test_conv_channel_mismatch_raises: Compare x.shape[1] with w.shape[1] before doing any math.
hints.test_conv_is_fast_enough: Avoid Python loops over N, F and C. im2col: gather patches into (N·H_out·W_out, C·KH·KW) and do one matmul with w.reshape(F, -1).T. numpy.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view helps.
hints.test_maxpool_forward_matches_reference: stride defaults to pool_size. Window (i, j) starts at row i·stride, column j·stride; take the max over its last two axes.
hints.test_maxpool_backward_routes_to_argmax: Only the max element of each window receives that window's gradient. Everything else gets 0.
hints.test_maxpool_backward_overlapping_window: With stride < pool_size one input can be the max of several windows. Add (+=) every contribution into dx.
